executiveSummary.text: Risk tone is no longer one-way risk-on: S&P 500 -0.52%, Nasdaq -0.32%, Dow -0.51%, VIX 15.19 (+6.6%) as oil and long yields rose. Base case: 50% choppy soft-landing/risk-on, 30% rates/oil valuation air-pocket, 15% inflation-reacceleration scare, 5% liquidity/geopolitical shock. Confidence: medium.

Rates are again the main transmission channel: latest FRED 2Y/10Y/30Y were 4.17%/4.68%/5.25% as of Aug 14, while market proxies put 10Y near 4.72% and 30Y near 5.31% on Aug 17. Higher long-end yields pressure REITs and long-duration AI multiples even if earnings demand remains solid.

Oil is the fresh macro shock: WTI +3.1% to ~$85 and Brent +3.0% to ~$91 after US-Iran peace hopes faded and Hormuz/tanker traffic concerns re-entered pricing. Second order: higher inflation breakevens can delay Fed cuts; third order: duration equities and Singapore REITs remain capped.

AI/semis remain bifurcated rather than broken: MU +4.1%, AMAT +5.6%, LRCX +3.5% outperformed on AI memory/equipment demand and positioning, while MSFT -3.0% and META -3.5% lagged with megacap/hyperscaler credit and regulatory worries. KL scarcity thesis intact, but valuation discipline matters.

Scarcity assets worked: gold futures +2.1%, COPX +1.9%, SLV +1.9%, URNM +1.8%. This was not a lazy safe-haven trade alone: softer USD, geopolitical oil inflation, real-yield sensitivity, and central-bank/institutional positioning all matter.

usGlobal.what: US equities opened the week lower with volatility up but not panicky.
usGlobal.why: Oil and long-end Treasury yields rose together; that is a worse mix for multiples than an isolated growth scare.
usGlobal.implication: Keep risk exposure, but expect more factor dispersion and less broad beta tailwind.

ratesMacro.what: Long-duration rates remain the marginal price-setter.
ratesMacro.why: 30Y yield proxy moved above 5.3%; FRED latest 10Y real yield was 2.41%. Real discount rates are high enough to compress long-duration cash-flow assets.
ratesMacro.implication: AI and REIT entries should be staged; do not chase green semicap days if yields keep rising.

asiaSingapore.what: Singapore market held up better than US beta; ES3 +0.97%, DBS +1.79%, Keppel +3.04%, Sembcorp +2.40%, UOB -1.60%.
asiaSingapore.why: Banks remain supported by high nominal rates; infrastructure/energy-linked names benefit from scarcity/power narratives; REITs remain capped by global long rates.
asiaSingapore.implication: Singapore dividend sleeve remains ballast, but REIT recovery needs a clearer long-yield rollover.

commodities.what: Oil, gold, silver and commodity equities rose.
commodities.why: Middle East supply-risk premium returned while USD was slightly softer; gold also benefits from central-bank/institutional demand but can be hurt if real yields spike further.
commodities.implication: KL's scarcity sleeve is doing its job as an inflation/geopolitical shock diversifier.

geopolitics.why: Reuters/Yahoo-reported fading peace hopes and slower tanker traffic create a direct oil/inflation/rates transmission path.
geopolitics.implication: Watch whether oil strength broadens into breakevens and Fed-cut repricing; that would hit duration assets.

moves.why: Semicap/equipment rebound after prior expectation-driven selling; fresh screen showed AMAT among manufacturing/AI exporters moving sharply, with AI hardware demand still resilient.
moves.implication: Supports KL's equipment scarcity sleeve; this is thesis-confirming unless order/capex cancellations appear.
moves.action: HOLD; ADD only on 10-15% drawdowns or if earnings confirm order acceleration without multiple expansion. Invalidate if memory/foundry capex is cut.

moves.why: AI memory/HBM optimism and analyst upgrades continued; memory remains the tightest bottleneck in the AI stack.
moves.implication: Positive second order for equipment suppliers and HBM supply chain; cyclical risk remains if DRAM pricing peaks.
moves.action: HOLD/WATCH; add only after volatility or confirmed HBM contract visibility. Trim if price action becomes parabolic versus earnings revisions.

moves.why: Megacap/hyperscaler weakness as higher yields and reports of creditworthiness/AI-capex concern hit duration cash flows; Meta also faces renewed regulatory/AI-positioning scrutiny in fresh headlines.
moves.implication: Not thesis damage yet: cloud/AI capex remains strategic, but financing/ROIC scrutiny is rising. Third order: hyperscaler cost discipline could affect semicap order timing.
moves.action: HOLD; ADD only if free-cash-flow durability remains intact and selloff is valuation-led. Invalidate if AI capex starts cannibalising core margins without revenue proof.

moves.why: Singapore infrastructure/power scarcity names outperformed; no single 24h company-specific thesis break found.
moves.implication: Reinforces KL's power/grid bottleneck exposure in Singapore sleeve.
moves.action: HOLD; avoid chasing after +3% days unless project/order news changes earnings base.

moves.what: Commodity sleeve: GLD +1.00%, COPX +1.91%, SLV +1.86%, URNM +1.80%; gold futures +2.13%, oil +3%.
moves.why: Oil/geopolitical risk, softer USD, and metals scarcity supported the sleeve.
moves.implication: Diversification benefit is working; watch real yields because they can offset gold even during geopolitical stress.
moves.action: HOLD; ADD to copper/uranium only on pullbacks or confirmed supply deficit data. Trim if oil shock forces disorderly risk-off/liquidity squeeze.

thesisImpact.what: AI scarcity chain remains intact but less forgiving.
thesisImpact.why: Memory and equipment rose while hyperscalers sold off; the market is separating suppliers with near-term bottleneck pricing from platforms carrying giant capex budgets.
thesisImpact.implication: Own the bottlenecks, but require ROIC proof from capex spenders.
thesisImpact.action: Maintain barbell; rebalance only on extremes.

narratives.title: Oil/rates are the key regime test
narratives.description: If oil strength feeds inflation expectations, the Fed reaction function tightens just as long-end supply concerns keep yields high. That is the path from geopolitical headline to equity multiple compression.
narratives.source: Yahoo Finance/Reuters snippets; FRED/Yahoo market data
narratives.priceImpact: Negative for duration equities and REITs; positive for energy/scarcity assets until demand destruction appears.

narratives.title: AI bifurcation: bottleneck winners vs capex funders
narratives.description: MU/AMAT/LRCX strength alongside MSFT/META weakness shows investors still like AI supply scarcity but are questioning whether hyperscaler capex earns adequate returns.
narratives.source: Brave Search fresh results; yfinance market data
narratives.priceImpact: Constructive for semicap/memory if orders hold; valuation risk for expensive platforms.

narratives.title: Singapore barbell is functioning
narratives.description: Banks and infrastructure held up while REITs lagged the rates impulse. This matches KL's need for income ballast plus scarcity exposure.
narratives.priceImpact: Stable income sleeve; REIT upside delayed until long rates fall.

secondOrderEffects.text: Oil up -> headline inflation and breakevens risk up -> Fed cut odds fall / long yields rise -> REITs and long-duration AI multiples de-rate even if earnings estimates do not immediately move.
secondOrderEffects.implication: Avoid adding aggressively to REITs or richly valued AI until the oil/yield impulse fades.

secondOrderEffects.text: Hyperscaler capex scrutiny -> investors demand proof of AI monetisation -> suppliers with immediate bottleneck pricing can outperform initially, but a later capex discipline cycle could slow equipment orders.
secondOrderEffects.implication: Semicap strength is positive but not risk-free; watch order guidance, not only share prices.

secondOrderEffects.text: Gold up with USD soft and oil risk is constructive, but if real yields jump faster than inflation expectations, gold can stall despite geopolitical headlines.
secondOrderEffects.implication: Treat GLD as portfolio insurance/scarcity ballast, not a one-way crisis trade.

investment.thesis: Maintain the AI scarcity stack: TSM/equipment/HBM/EDA plus grid and metals.
investment.trigger: Add only on 10-15% sleeve drawdowns, confirmed capex/order strength, or valuation reset without thesis break.
investment.whyNow: Market is rewarding bottlenecks but punishing unfunded/uncertain AI ROI; selectivity is increasing.
investment.invalidator: Hyperscaler capex cuts, HBM oversupply, foundry utilisation rollover, or export controls that materially impair revenue.

investment.thesis: Keep Singapore banks/infrastructure as ballast, but be patient on REITs.
investment.trigger: REIT add trigger: US 10Y sustainably below ~4.3% or SG refinancing spreads improve; banks trim trigger: NIM compression plus credit costs rising.
investment.whyNow: High long rates support banks but cap REIT duration; Keppel/Sembcorp align with power scarcity.
investment.invalidator: Singapore recession/credit cycle or structural fall in bank profitability.

trading.thesis: Do not chase semicap gap-ups; use volatility to scale.
trading.trigger: Buy partials only after failed breakdown/reclaim days or post-earnings order confirmation; avoid adding after +3-6% single-day moves.
trading.whyNow: AMAT/LRCX/MU moved sharply and positioning can reverse if yields keep rising.
trading.invalidator: SOX breadth rolls over with rising yields and weak guidance.

trading.thesis: Oil shock hedge only if transmission broadens.
trading.trigger: If Brent holds >$90 and breakevens rise for several sessions, energy/scarcity hedges remain useful; if oil fades below ~$85 Brent, treat as headline premium unwind.
trading.whyNow: Hormuz/Iran risk is directly in crude pricing again.

watchlist.thesis: US 30Y yield above 5.3% is the stress line.
watchlist.trigger: Sustained move higher with VIX >18 and Nasdaq underperformance.
watchlist.whyNow: Long-end yields are already close to the level pressuring duration assets.
watchlist.invalidator: 30Y falls back below 5.1% with stable oil.

watchlist.thesis: Hyperscaler AI ROI narrative could shift from growth to credit/capex discipline.
watchlist.trigger: More headlines on debt funding, lower capex guidance, or cloud margin pressure at MSFT/AMZN/GOOG/META.
watchlist.whyNow: MSFT/META sold off while semicap bottlenecks rose.
watchlist.invalidator: Revenue acceleration and margin stability despite capex.

riskWatch.name: Oil-inflation-rate shock
riskWatch.description: Brent near $91 with Hormuz/Iran risk can flow into inflation expectations and long yields.
riskWatch.mitigation: Keep cash dry powder; avoid over-adding duration; retain scarcity/commodity diversifiers.

riskWatch.name: AI capex/credit repricing
riskWatch.description: Market may demand clearer returns from hyperscaler AI spending; suppliers can lag later if capex discipline rises.
riskWatch.mitigation: Prefer bottlenecks with pricing power; watch order guidance and FCF, not narrative only.

riskWatch.name: REIT duration trap
riskWatch.description: Singapore REITs can stay cheap for longer if global long rates remain high.
riskWatch.mitigation: Stage entries; require yield rollover/refinancing improvement before size.

keyEvents.text: Yahoo Finance: US stocks fell Monday as oil and Treasury yields jumped; VIX 15.19 (+6.6%).
Reuters/Yahoo: oil rose as US-Iran peace hopes faded and Hormuz/tanker traffic worries persisted.
FRED latest: 2Y 4.17%, 10Y 4.68%, 30Y 5.25%, 10Y TIPS real yield 2.41% as of Aug 14; live proxies moved higher Aug 17.
Portfolio scan: abnormal moves in AMAT, LRCX, MU, MSFT, META, Keppel and commodity ETFs.

bottomLine.whatMatters: The key variable is not whether equities were down modestly; it is whether oil strength and long yields persist together. That mix can change the discount-rate regime for AI, REITs and broad risk assets.
bottomLine.whatToDo: Keep the barbell. Hold AI/scarcity winners, avoid chasing +3-6% semicap days, reserve cash for yield/oil-driven air pockets, and require REIT yield confirmation before adding size.
bottomLine.whatToIgnore: Ignore one-day portfolio P/L noise unless it is tied to order cuts, hyperscaler capex reversal, credit stress, or a sustained oil/rates shock.
